content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged Chinese pangolin frame. Host frame: the chinese pangolin sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a axolotl and a chinese pangolin. Head of the chinese pangolin, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: behavior: follows head/brain donor per RC-R5-07: solitary nocturnal pangolin foraging; body: host pangolin frame and scale armor throughout; axolotl tissue only as separate surface patches, blend only at patch edges; axolotl skin in a few large patches over the back and flanks, at full strength with clean edges, color and surface unchanged inside each patch; chinese pangolin coat everywhere else; ears: small pangolin ears; no axolotl ear tissue; face: pangolin narrow snout and small mouth for ant/termite feeding; feet: pangolin clawed digging feet; head: pangolin head tissue including brain; limbs: short powerful pangolin legs with digging claws; support unchanged at host size; skull: pangolin skull; tail: muscular scaled pangolin tail for balance; host tissue throughout; plain coat, no stripes or spots. Coat texture flows along the body outline. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (river forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Composing hybrid creature illustration**
I'm planning a natural history illustration that merges a pangolin's scaled body, snout, ears, claws, and tail with smooth pink axolotl patches on the back and flanks, keeping the head fully pangolin.
**Drafting axolotl-pangolin image**
I'm preparing a detailed side three-quarter view with countershading, smooth axolotl skin texture, four legs with pangolin claws, and two patches on the upper back and flank against a plain light background.
**Refining texture smoothness**
I'm adjusting the illustration so the patches read as smooth skin instead of scales, keeping the axolotl-pangolin hybrid look while softening the surface detail.
